title: Henry 'Red' Hicks, the neat trombonist
summary: Hicks came with Benny Carter's band, played sweet legit trombone and kept his suit unwrinkled on long bus rides; the nickname Red had nothing to do with red hair.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well, he came here with Benny Carter's band, I think.
The same band the rest of them boys was with. You're getting me mixed up on my bands now....
Well, Hicks was with the Mills Blue Rhythm Band, too.
I know he was with the Blue Rhythm, but I mean when he first come here... He came with a band, you know.
Well, they called him "Red" Hicks. Was that...?
Yeah. But was that because he had freckles or light hair or something?

That's why they called him Red! That's the only reason I see. It wasn't nothin' red about him. But Red was just a nickname, Red Hicks. He didn't have no red hair. No, the only reason can I see is because he was black.
Oh, he was more on the sweet style, the legitimate style. But he could play nice trombone, very good. Good musician. Neat as a pin...

Oh yeah, he was a good reader. Neat as a pin. He'd sit in the bus, have on his suit, you know, creased and one-thing-or-another... He'd sit in the bus, and would go... He could travel from here to Chicago, and get out of the bus, and wouldn't have a wrinkle in his suit.
